extraction.name: AMASS
extraction.description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common framework and parameterization. It is intended to support animation, visualization, and training data generation for deep learning.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors used an OptiTrack mocap system synchronized with a 4D scanning system to capture subjects with 67 markers, and for AMASS they amassed 15 mocap datasets from publicly available downloads, privately obtained datasets, and datasets recorded by the authors themselves; they then used MoSh++ to map marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters, with manual inspection to correct or hold out mislabeled/swapped markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Due to swapped and mislabeled markers, the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problematic cases.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mocap marker data from 15 datasets, including synchronized mocap and 4D scan data for SSM, with subjects wearing 67 markers (and a 46-marker subset used for evaluation).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The source motion capture datasets are heterogeneous and often narrowly focused on particular motion classes, which may bias the combined archive toward the motions and subject populations represented in those archival datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset inherits limitations from archival marker-based mocap, including varying markersets and laboratory-specific procedures; the paper also notes that previous methods were limited by incompatible body representations and that some users may ignore shape/soft-tissue if only pose is needed. The dataset is intended for research and training data generation, not as a complete representation of all human motion.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is positioned to enable animation and computer vision research, including synthetic training data generation for computer vision tasks.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes human motion and body-related attributes such as body shape, pose, soft-tissue dynamics, hand articulation, and subject identity/variation across 346 subjects.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, validation/fine-tuning, animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning/computer vision. The paper also notes that users interested only in pose can ignore body shape and soft tissue deformations.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community, and the authors state they will continue to expand it and support new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
